date: 2026-11 (between 2 and 6 Nov; the page gives no day)
title: A tool result would have handed a vault key to the model
what_happened: In the policy studio, a browser chat with tools, the create_vault tool returned a new vault's read key as a tool result, so the key would have reached the model's provider.
what_the_abp_said: Barrier: the person's yes on each write.
what_we_did: The developer agent's own review caught it; every vault write now asks the person to confirm and the key stays out of the model's context.
quote: now every vault write asks the person to confirm, and the key stays out of the model's context

date: 2026-11 (between 2 and 6 Nov; the page gives no day)
title: A reviewer held a draft that would have published a token's value
what_happened: A team member's vault agent drafted a board issue that named a vault and said a token had the same value.
what_we_did: A code-reviewer sub-agent that runs before every push held it; only the hold and its record were released, and the work stayed local until fixed.
quote: only the hold and its record were released, the work stayed local until fixed

title: An agent undid another agent's key entry; the sealing tool now refuses
what_happened: A helper agent committed the shared keys file from an older copy and undid the mark that another agent's key had ended, so an ended key would have looked live; it noticed and restored the entry itself.
what_the_abp_said: The ABP recorded that nothing else would have caught it (WS-152).
what_we_did: seal.mjs now refuses ended keys and entries changed from another person's account.
quote: seal.mjs now refuses ended keys and entries changed from another person's account
note: Our own pages disagree on the time it took: the in-action page says 'three hours', newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/web-summit-part-five.html says 'Within the hour'. Published unresolved. Date 4 Nov from part five (the day it covers).

title: Three agents were told to commit as the conductor
what_happened: The prompts of the ABP, sgit and project-manager agents were copies of the conductor's, telling them to commit as the conductor and run its wake.
what_the_abp_said: Found by the ABP agent and filed as WS-89.
what_we_did: Fixed in two steps; the ABP agent reopened the issue when the first fix fell short.

title: An agent pushed with the operator's own token
what_happened: The CRM agent pushed using the operator's own SG/Send token rather than one of its own.
what_the_abp_said: An agent pushed with the operator's own SG/Send token (the CRM agent's ABP).
what_we_did: It stopped when Dinis said every agent should have its own token.
quote: it stopped when Dinis said every agent should have its own

title: A reviewer agent asked for a permission and got five fields
what_happened: A team member's reviewer agent needed to write the lead of one story on the newsroom's front page, a file owned by another agent under a deny-by-default ABP.
what_the_abp_said: Granted only the five S41 lead keys of front-page.json; it 'never' changes any other key or writes any other file under desks/correspondent/.
what_we_did: Dinis granted the narrow write in his own session, recorded in the grant with time and who granted it, for that one story only.
quote: can you give my reviewer@ permission to write only the five S41 lead fields in front-page.json?
note: Outcome list has no 'granted'; found-fixed is the nearest. Source read 16 Nov 2026 (policies.json v1.14.0, updated 2026-11-16T20:05Z).

date: observed 05:47 UTC (day not given); still proposed on 2026-11-16
title: The conductor needs a permission to hand a role over
what_happened: To hand a role to a new session the conductor needs create_session and update_trigger; one update_trigger call was observed, logged and not blocked (the hooks run in observe mode).
what_the_abp_said: denied until Dinis grants it here, ideally only against a handover order signed with his key
what_we_did: The ABP agent proposed the relaxation to Dinis; it is written down, not granted.
quote: denied until Dinis grants it here, ideally only against a handover order signed with his key

title: The backup agent waits for a written grant instead of connecting
what_happened: The backup agent's plan calls for Google Drive, but its ABP allows no connector unless Dinis grants it in writing.
what_the_abp_said: No connector at all ... unless Dinis grants it in writing in this file.
what_we_did: The ABP agent proposed a Drive grant, write-only to one folder Dinis names; meanwhile the agent keeps its bundle in the ephemeral container.
quote: backup@ waits on a written grant

title: Agents can start agents, and the only barrier is a sentence
what_happened: Every session measured in Dinis's account holds the tools to create scheduled tasks and new sessions; on 6 November a conductor on a second account started moved agents' sessions one at a time, at his word.
what_the_abp_said: The only barrier is the sentence "never create a scheduled task, a session or a workflow" in each prompt.
what_we_did: Recorded as a capability that could do real damage; it stays open in the explorer phase, with the step that would close it.
quote: A rule, not a control: the one capability that turns one mistake into many.

title: A rule changed behaviour; only a boundary changed what the agent read
what_happened: One real agent did a support job for a made-up company in a mock world six times under pressure (a phishing mail, hidden instructions, pasted secrets): with nothing in its way, with a rule, and with technical barriers in the gateway.
what_the_abp_said: a rule (an expectation) changes behaviour but not reach; a boundary changes reach, and the job still gets done.
what_we_did: Ran it as an experiment on our own mock system and published the result; the next step is a stand demo of the same.
quote: the difference is what reaches the agent
note: The company and world are invented (a mock). The screenshot's text says 'levels 0 and 1' (the page's term for the set-ups, not a score); the developer may prefer to crop it.

title: A conductor set up other agents' scheduled tasks from its own session
what_happened: Building a talk in a day, the conductor set up all four scheduled tasks from its own session, including three that belonged to other members.
what_the_abp_said: A task belongs to the session it fires into.
what_we_did: Dinis corrected it and the three for other members were disabled before any fired.
quote: the three for other members were disabled before any fired
note: Same screenshot as talk-installs-refused (the article's 'What went wrong' list).

title: The sandbox refused two installs; the tools were vendored instead
what_happened: An agent tried to install a command-line tool and to run another team's script as code from outside; the sandbox's classifier refused both.
what_we_did: Every tool the members run is now vendored in the repository, with the key tool's hash checked.
quote: The sandbox's classifier refused to install a command-line tool and to run another team's script as code from outside.

date: 2026-10-29T18:44 (London, which is UTC on that date)
title: The conductor stopped every agent sixteen minutes before the talk
what_happened: With Dinis's usage limit at 95%, the conductor put every member on hold at 18:44; the talk ran as it stood.
what_the_abp_said: anyone may stop, and nobody needs permission to.
what_we_did: Nothing to fix: the stop rule worked as designed.
quote: the rule worked as designed: anyone may stop, and nobody needs permission to
note: The article gives 18:44 without a zone; the talk was in London, which was on GMT (UTC) on 29 Oct 2026.

title: The policy said agents could not attach files; one did
what_happened: An agent that needed to send a signed letter found that the Gmail connector's draft tools accept an attachments array, proved it with a 17 KB signed PDF, and wrote it up; Dinis sent the draft by hand.
what_the_abp_said: Nothing: the policy did not bother to forbid what seemed impossible.
what_we_did: Sending attachments is now held by an admin rule in the mail system (outbound attachment compliance strips or rejects), per the article's enforcement table.
quote: A policy written from the documentation was wrong.
note: Before the Web Summit team: Dinis's own two-identity setup. The article's table states the admin rule as today's enforcement (article v1.2.1, updated 2 Oct 2026); we did not check the admin console.
